additions.description: GET /api/v1/password-recovery-html/{email} endpoint is implemented as a formal route
additions.reasoning: The specification mentions retrieving password-recovery HTML content only as a step in a test scenario, not as a formally specified endpoint with defined behavior. The spec never lists it as a required route.

omissions.description: GET /api/v1/items/{item_id} does not enforce ownership-based access control: a non-superuser can read items they do not own without receiving 400 'Not enough permissions'
omissions.reasoning: The specification states: 'Attempt to read the created item using the access token of the second user. Verify that the response status code is 400 and the response body contains a detail field with the value "Not enough permissions"'. The code has no ownership check in read_item and returns the item to any authenticated user.

omissions.description: POST /api/v1/users/signup returns detail 'User with this email already exists' instead of 'The user with this email already exists in the system'
omissions.reasoning: The specification states: 'Verify the response body field "detail" equals "The user with this email already exists in the system"'. The code raises HTTPException(status_code=400, detail='User with this email already exists') which does not match the required message.

omissions.description: The password recovery email is not actually delivered to the mailcatcher service via SMTP; the code incorrectly POSTs a JSON payload to the mailcatcher HTTP API
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires verifying 'that an email was actually sent to the correct recipient via the mailcatcher service (verify via GET http://localhost:1080/messages)'. Mailcatcher receives emails via SMTP (port 1025), not via HTTP POST to /messages. The code's send_recovery_email posts JSON to http://localhost:1080/messages which is not a valid way to inject mail into mailcatcher, so the email will not appear when checking GET http://localhost:1080/messages.
